title: QBR: Activation & Ops Sprint for Tiered Upgrades
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working QBR + renewal/upsell activation sprint doc for mid-to-large customers that are candidates for tiered upgrades: moving from hosted to Dedicated, upgrading Dedicated capacity tiers, or migrating to Private deployments and/or purchasing premium SLA add-ons. Audience: CSMs, Solutions Eng, Account Execs, and the Platform/Infra on-call or solutions owners who will scope technical gating items.

High-level outcome (one-liner):
End the QBR with a prioritized expansion plan (Recommended SKU/commit, estimated cost delta, technical gating list, milestone dates) and a handoff ticket to Solutions Engineering + Sales Ops to create an amendment/PO.

Pre-read (sent 3 business days before QBR):
- 90d usage dump (tokens by model, avg tokens/request, daily peak TPS)
- Cost vs committed spend and overage history
- Latency and error SLO trends (p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rate)
- Recent incidents and mitigation notes (links to postmortems)
- Customer business context and new projects (product roadmap bullets)

QBR agenda (60–75 minutes recommended):
1) 0–10m: Welcome, attendees, objectives for this meeting (CSM)
2) 10–20m: Business update — customer product milestones, timelines (Customer PO)
3) 20–35m: Usage & performance review (CSM/SE)
   - Key metrics: daily active apps, requests/day, tokens/day, peak concurrency, model mix, p95 latency, error %
   - Highlight: any sustained growth (>3x over 60d) or repeat rate-limit events
4) 35–50m: Risk & reliability summary (SRE/SE)
   - Incident recap, root cause, mitigations, and recommended next steps (e.g., dedicated pool, autoscale config)
5) 50–65m: Expansion options (CSM + AE) — prioritized by score (see rubric below)
6) 65–75m: Next steps, owners, and timeline (CSM to capture commitments)

Pre-QBR checklist (CSM):
- [ ] Validate attendee list includes engineering decision maker + procurement contact
- [ ] Run automated health report and attach to pre-read
- [ ] Pull cost / commit vs usage forecast (Finance Ops template link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Create a TL;DR recommended SKU and rationale to present

Expansion scoring rubric (quick, additive 0–3 per dimension):
- Usage Momentum (0 none - 3 high): sustained volume growth, peak concurrency trends, burst frequency
- Reliability Impact (0 - 3): number/severity of incidents tied to capacity or noisy neighbors
- Business Sensitivity (0 - 3): PII/regulatory needs, legal/compliance drivers, procurement readiness
- Economic Upside (0 - 3): clear unit economics improvement (eg: Dedicated lowers per-token cost by X%)
- Sales Readiness (0 - 3): contract appetite, budget cycle alignment, champion strength
Total 0–15. Prioritize scores >=10 for immediate outreach.

Example expansion recommendations (boilerplate language):
- Dedicated Upsize recommendation: "Recommend Dedicated Tier C (8x baseline) with standard autoscale and 4-week canary. Rationale: p95 latency instability and sustained 2.5x weekday peak; expected 20% cost savings on high-volume paths."
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) recommendation: "Recommend Private Basic (VPC) with KMS integration and audit logging. Trigger: legal requirement for data residency + IAM SAML integration request."
- Premium SLA add-on: "Recommend Enterprise SLA (10ms p95 target, 99.95% uptime, priority incident queue) for teams with revenue-impacting features and 24/7 support window."

Technical gating checklist (for SE/SRE sprint):
- [ ] Network: confirm CIDR allowlist, peering or VPN, and bandwidth estimates
- [ ] Auth: SAML/OIDC integration plan, KMS/HSM key management checklist
- [ ] Data residency: confirm storage/backups region mapping and encryption at rest in scope
- [ ] Telemetry: attach tracing+logs to customer-specific project (retain 90d for SLA upgrades)
- [ ] Load tests: schedule 1–2 staged load tests with baseline and spike scenarios (owner, date)
- [ ] Rollback policy: define fallback model variant or burst to hosted pool

Pilot & canary timeline (recommended cadence):
- Week 0: Kickoff + network/auth prep
- Week 1–2: Provision Dedicated/Private environment + smoke tests
- Week 3: Internal load tests, adjust autoscale/batching configuration
- Week 4: Customer canary traffic (10–20% of production)
- Week 5–6: Ramp to full traffic or negotiate staged commit

Commercial & contract notes (CSM + AE guide):
- Pricing levers: committed throughput, priority support seats, retention/telemetry retention, model quantization/accelerator tiers
- One-off fees: private deployment setup, dedicated burst capacity, audit/compliance attestation
- Negotiation anchors: propose a 6–9 month ramp with quarterly usage reconciliation versus full 12-month commit
- PO language snippet: "Redwood Inference amendment for Dedicated capacity / Private deployment — scope, target start date, SLOs, invoice schedule."

Customer-facing outreach templates (short, editable):
- Email subject: "QBR follow-up: proposed Dedicated pilot & SLA options for <Account>"
- Short email body: "Hi <Name>, thanks for the time today. Based on our QBR, we recommend piloting Dedicated Tier C with a 4–week canary to address p95 latency and predictable capacity. Attached is a one-page estimate and technical gating checklist. Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to align on network and auth? — Ava"
- Call script snippets: "Confirm: who’s owning network peering? Who signs the amendment? Any procurement dates in the next 30–60 days?"

Renewal & expansion tracker (mini table you can paste into your tracker)

| Account | Current SKU | Renewal Date | Expansion Recommendation | Estimated ARR Upsell | Technical Owner | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Acme Corp | Hosted S | 2026-06-15 | Dedicated Tier B pilot | $120k | Jordan Lee | pre-read sent |
| Beta Retail | Dedicated B | 2026-04-01 | Increase to Dedicated C + SLA | $85k | Ravi Patel | in_discussion |
| FinCo | Hosted L | 2026-09-30 | Private VPC + KMS | $220k | Sofia Morales | compliance_review |
(When pasting into tracker: convert to row-per-account, use one-line action item per account.)

Risk mitigations and fallback plans: practical advice
- If network/VPN delays occur: offer interim hosted-tier burst capacity and set up rate-limiting guardrails
- If procurement stalls: propose a time-limited pilot order for a credit-backed trial
- If performance regressions post-migration: immediate rollback to hosted variant + priority incident bridge

Open questions to resolve during the QBR (capture live):
- What is the procurement timeline and PO owner?
- Are there contractual terms (data residency, SOC2 artifacts) needed for legal approval?
- Which internal stakeholders need a technical walkthrough (SRE, infra, security)?

Post-QBR immediate handoff template (CSM -> SE + AE):
Subject: "Hand-off: <Account> QBR expansion package — recommended path + technical gates"
Body bullets to include: summary (1–2 lines), recommended SKU, forecast ARR, technical gating checklist items with owners, target pilot start date, and sales ops ticket ID. Attach pre-read and cost model.

Notes, hypotheses, and areas for testing (working):
- Hypothesis A: moving large-model inference to Dedicated reduces tail latency variance by >30% due to isolated GPU pools
- Hypothesis B: lightweight quantization + batch tuning will reduce per-token cost by up to 15% for embed-heavy workloads with no measurable impact on relevance in our eval set
- Plan to measure: run A/B on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks during ramp and evaluate p95/p99 and top-5 generation disagreement rates

Appendix: quick checklist for premium SLA signups
- SLA sign-up items: invoice cadence, SLO definitions, incident contact list, runbook access, escalation matrix, audit evidence folder (SOC2/SOC3/KMS attestation)
- Required internal approvals: Security review, Finance billing exception (if pre-paid credits), Infra capacity reservation

Versioning and doc maintenance:
- This is a living template; please add notes after each QBR with lessons learned and link to the AE amendment once executed.

---
Document history (changes):

Quick action (for this file): CSMs — duplicate into your account folder, update the mini tracker lines and attach the usage pre-read before scheduling.
